title: Review rhythm and the annual review
objectives: Run the monthly, quarterly and annual review rhythm.
Judge a PMS on 3+ years of after-fee returns.
Explain why account return can differ from strategy return.
body_md:
A PMS is judged on at least three years of after-fee returns against its benchmark, never on one quarter or on the strategy's headline number.

## Review rhythm

- Monthly: client receives the statement; we check for unusual trades, cash levels or large drawdowns.
- Quarterly: short call or note covering performance vs benchmark, portfolio changes and the manager's commentary.
- Annually: full review with the client, as below.

## Annual review agenda

- Client update: goals, liquidity needs, risk comfort, tax situation.
- Returns: the client's own account return, after all fees and expenses, vs benchmark and vs peers in the same strategy on APMI data.
- Risk: largest fall this year and since inception vs the benchmark's.
- Portfolio: concentration, turnover, style drift, cash calls.
- Manager: any change in fund manager, team, process or ownership.
- Costs: total fees paid in rupees, and tax generated by trading.
- Fit: is the PMS still the right share of the client's total portfolio? Rebalance if it has grown or shrunk too much.
- Decision: stay, top up, reduce or exit, recorded with reasons.
example: The factsheet shows +40% but the client's account returned 12%. The client joined late in the year and cash flows differed. You show the account's own after-fee return against the benchmark.
say: After all fees, your account is 3% a year ahead of its benchmark over three years.
Your own account's return can differ from the strategy's published return. Here is why.
never: Ignore the factsheet number, it doesn't matter.

check.q: On what basis should a PMS be judged?
o: Returns compared with a bank FD
3+ years of after-fee returns vs its benchmark
check.why: Never judge a PMS on one quarter or on the headline strategy number.

check.q: Factsheet shows +40%, but the client has made only 12%. Most likely reason?
o: The manager charged the client a hidden fee
Different entry timing, prices and cash flows
The client's stocks are different by mistake
check.why: Each account is built at a different time and price. Show the client their own after-fee account return.

check.q: How often should a PMS client receive a full review?
check.why: The review rhythm is monthly statements, quarterly updates and a full annual review.
